title: Approval queue — pricing variance & KMS onboarding readout
next_steps: Redwood to send DPA redline + annotated MSA excerpt by 2025-12-01
SE to schedule KMS connectivity dry-run (VPC peering + HSM handshake) week of 2025-12-08
Customer to review pricing variance sheet and confirm target commit by 2025-12-05
Schedule legal deep-dive if redlines exceed standard concessions (tentative 2025-12-03)
action_items: Alex Monroe: share detailed pricing scenarios including burst vs reserved commits (2025-11-28)
Priya Shah: provide KMS connectivity checklist and example Terraform for key rotation (2025-12-02)
Hannah Lee: flag any unusual DPA clauses and send preferred redlines (2025-12-01)
Markus Lind: validate HSM vendor compatibility and list required ciphers (2025-12-04)
header: Date: 2025-11-26T15:00Z | Duration: 54m | Attendees: Alex Monroe (Redwood AE); Priya Shah (Redwood SE); Jamie Ortega (SilverOak Procurement); Markus Lind (SilverOak Security); Hannah Lee (SilverOak Legal)
summary: Procurement/legal alignment call covering pricing variance paths, MSA/DPA redline expectations, and technical preflight for KMS/HSM onboarding. Consensus to push DPA redline by Dec 1, SE to run KMS dry-run week of Dec 8. Pricing options to be reviewed by customer procurement team next week.
topics: DPA redline expectations and data residency clauses
KMS/HSM onboarding: connectivity, ciphers, audit logs
transcript:
00:00 Alex Monroe: hey everybody thanks for joining, we got about 55 minutes, um quick roll call?
00:07 Jamie Ortega: yeah this is Jamie, thanks Alex, Markus and Hannah are here from our side.
00:12 Markus Lind: Markus on security, hi.
00:15 Priya Shah: hey all, Priya from Redwood SE.
00:18 Hannah Lee: Hannah, legal.
:-- Summary: Alex outlines agenda: pricing, DPA redlines, KMS onboarding.
02:12 Alex Monroe: ok first up pricing — we heard from procurement there's a variance requested on the reserved commit level, can you walk us through targeted monthly qps and burst patterns?
02:30 Jamie Ortega: yea so our peaks are end of month settlement windows, roughly 3x baseline for 45 minutes, otherwise steady low traffic. We're trying to avoid over-commit but need predictable unit costs for finance.
02:49 Priya Shah: what we're seeing — usually a mixed approach works: small reserved baseline for core ops and a burst bucket tacked on; we can do dynamic fallback to lower-cost model variants if the Dedicated pool is saturated.
03:10 Markus Lind: question on encryption — will keys stay in our KMS or you manage? We need customer-managed keys, HSM-backed.
03:22 Alex Monroe: yes customer-managed KMS supported, we do KMS integration for hosted and dedicated, there's a small egress op on the key handshake but we can outline.
03:35 Hannah Lee: on the DPA, we've got two items; data residency for EU person identifiers, and audit log retention at 7 years. your standard dpa lists 3 years.
03:53 Alex Monroe: totally fair. we can try to align to 7 years but might need a commercial uplift depending on retention costs — we'll flag that in pricing scenarios.
04:12 Jamie Ortega: ok so can you put that uplift number in the pricing table? we need finance to sign off.
04:20 Alex Monroe: yes i'll send three scenarios: minimal reserved (lower price, higher burst cost), midline commit (balanced), and enterprise reserved (discounted token rate) — i'll put the DPA retention uplift next to them.
05:01 Priya Shah: small note on runtime — if you do very large bursts the KV cache warm-up can add latency, we have prefix caching and warm-start but bursts still cost more initially.
05:20 Markus Lind: wait what's KV cache — I heard K V cash on the first pass earlier, haha.
05:27 Priya Shah: yeah it's KV cache, key-value cache for attention states; in our term it's k-v cache. apologies if the transcript picks that up weird.
05:40 Hannah Lee: legal aside: are we seeing any cross-border subprocessors? SilverOak requires a subprocessor list.
05:48 Alex Monroe: we maintain a subprocessors register; for private/VPC deployments it's zero additional subprocessors except cloud infra provider if hosted. We'll share the latest register in the redline packet.
06:10 Jamie Ortega: great. on MSA redlines — our legal team flagged indemnity carveouts and a requirement for SOC 2 type II evidence.
06:22 Hannah Lee: yes and SSO/SAML integration with our IdP must be in scope for RBAC enforcement.
06:29 Alex Monroe: SOC 2 attestation is standard, we can share the latest. SSO/SAML flows are supported; we also have SCIM for provisioning.
06:40 Markus Lind: KMS connectivity dry-run — if we bring our HSM (Thales) are there common pitfalls?
06:49 Priya Shah: common issues: firewall ports, TLS versions, mutual auth ciphers. We'll provide a concrete checklist and example Terraform. Also note rotation windows — if keys rotate at midnight you'll see transient auth failures unless cache refresh is configured.
07:14 Jamie Ortega: hm that last piece on rotation is a showstopper if not handled. we run daily rotation in prod.
07:21 Priya Shah: we can adjust rotation sync and implement a short grace window; we'll document it in the KMS runbook.
07:30 Hannah Lee: about SLA — our procurement requires a 99.9% P50/P95 SLA for inference latency and a financial rebate schedule for breaches.
07:41 Alex Monroe: Redwood provides per-route latency SLOs; commercial SLA with rebates is doable for Dedicated with reserved capacity. For hosted we have standard SLOs without rebate guarantees—that would be a pricing uplift.
07:58 Markus Lind: can we get an example of the wording for rollback / fallback? in high load we want deterministic behavior, not full failure.
08:08 Priya Shah: default behavior is automatic fallback to compatible model variant and queueing policy; we can include an explicit clause that in the event of sustained overload we will route to queued responses with a guaranteed retry window.
08:24 Jamie Ortega: ok good — procurement wants that in the MSA.
08:30 Hannah Lee: financing question — what's the minimum commit for enterprise discounted rate?
08:36 Alex Monroe: the enterprise tier typically starts at 150k tokens/month reserved or equivalent commit; we can show a sliding scale.
08:46 Jamie Ortega: that number helps. we'll run a cost model.
09:01 Alex Monroe: switching back to DPA redlines — Hannah, can you confirm the list of non-negotiables so we can try to pre-accept?
09:12 Hannah Lee: top items: 1) 7-year audit log retention, 2) SSO/SAML + SCIM support, 3) Customer-managed KMS with HSM, 4) Subprocessor transparency, 5) Clear indemnity ceilings. Anything outside those may need exec signoff.
09:34 Alex Monroe: ok we'll try to surface solutions for those first four in the redline package; indemnity we'll surface for commercial review.
09:45 Priya Shah: technical note: HSM ciphers — Markus if you can send the exact Thales firmware and required TLS ciphers, we'll validate compatibility.
09:56 Markus Lind: will do, list to follow by Friday.
10:03 Jamie Ortega: timeline — procurement needs contract in early Dec to make the board cycle.
10:10 Alex Monroe: understood. our working target is DPA/MSA redline package to you by 2025-12-01, pricing scenarios 2025-11-28, and KMS dry-run second week of December.
10:25 Hannah Lee: we'll try to prioritize our redlines the same week. if we have substantive asks we'll escalate.
10:34 Alex Monroe: any blockers on our side? Priya?
10:37 Priya Shah: nothing blocking; just need Markus firmware and the customer's KMS endpoint + health-check creds (ephemeral) for dry-run.
10:47 Jamie Ortega: we'll provide a scoped ID and allowlist several IPs, security will coordinate with Priya.
10:53 Alex Monroe: perfect. quick recap and owners — send pricing, draft DPA redline, KMS checklist and terraform, dry-run scheduling.
11:05 Hannah Lee: thanks all, appreciate the clarity.
11:08 Alex Monroe: thanks team, we'll sync next week if anything pops.
11:12 [meeting ends]
